title: Session benchlet: quick inference runs & notes
content:
One-line purpose: ephemeral sheet to track small runs, note anomalies, and capture quick config changes to try later. Not cleaned up; notes to self.

Columns (copied into a proper CSV later):
id | date | model | variant | quant | gpu | batch | seq_in | seq_out | tokens | p50_ms | p95_ms | p99_ms | throughput_tok/s | cost_per_1k_usd | notes | next_steps

Rows (most recent at top):
2026-02-17-06 | 2026-02-17 | vicuna-13b | fp16 | none | A10G | 4 | 64 | 256 | 320 | 42 | 180 | 520 | 1280 | 0.85 | output OK, occasional long tail on prompt with context refill | try kv-cache warmup; measure cold vs warm
2026-02-15-03 | 2026-02-15 | ggml-13b | int8 | 8bit | T4 | 8 | 32 | 128 | 190 | 75 | 420 | 1120 | 890 | 0.26 | cheaper but high p99 on T4 under >40 concurrent | reduce batch to 4; isolate network noise (host CPU spikes)
2025-12-01-11 | 2025-12-01 | redwood-small-7b | q4f16 | q4f16 | A100 | 16 | 16 | 64 | 85 | 21 | 110 | 300 | 4200 | 0.12 | great throughput; small degradation on long prompts >1024 | add regression test for >2048 tokens
2025-11-15-02 | 2025-11-15 | llama2-70b | bf16 | none | A100 | 1 | 128 | 512 | 640 | 95 | 420 | 1600 | 760 | 3.4 | baseline high cost; used for quality comparison | try mixed batching with redwood-small 7b fallback

Quick observations / heuristics:
- p99 is where production pain is: even small config/host noise spikes it up dramatically. Capture machine-level metrics next time (nvidia-smi, cpu, disk io).
- Larger batch sizes help throughput but can hurt p95/p99 unpredictably on shared hosts; dedicated pools are better.
- Quantized models (q4f16/int8) cut cost but sometimes produce higher CPU pre/post-processing overhead; measure end-to-end time with wall clock.

Notes-to-self (actionable):
- Instrument run that produced id 2026-02-17-06 with kv-cache warm/unwarm profiles. Re-run with warm cache 5x and cold cache runs 5x and record both.
- Reproduce T4 int8 run with constrained CPU cgroup to check if host CPU interferes.
- Add a small spike detector to local runner: if p95 > baseline*3, capture trace and logs automatically.

Scratch area (ideas, rough):
- Short-run A/B: use a lightweight eval set (10 prompts) to compare quality between q4f16 vs fp16 for redwood-small-7b. Save diffs and a small rubric.
- Try batch=2 + async streaming to reduce tail latency for interactive use-case.

References / quick links:
- Notes on kv-cache behavior: confluence.redwood/inference/kv-cache-ops (WIP)
- GH PR: https://github.com/redwood/runtime/pull/842 (perf kernels patch)
- JIRA INF-1297: 'reduce p99 jitter on T4 hosts'

Unresolved questions (for later):
- How much does CPU affinity (isolcpus) vs cgroup limit reduce p99? Quick experiment design: run 10x with default, 10x with isolcpus pinned, 10x with cgroup limit - compare p95/p99.
- Is network jitter causing the 420ms p99 spikes on shared T4 instances? Need tcpdump + host-level queuing stats.

Log of quick CLI commands used (copy/paste later):
- ./run_infer --model redwood-small-7b --device a100 --batch 16 --seq-in 16 --seq-out 64 --log-trace perf-20251101.json
- docker run --cpuset-cpus=2-7 --shm-size=1g runtime-image:latest ./serve --port 5005

End of benchlet. Keep this as a short-lived scratchpad; merge findings into eng-serving-runtime/bench-notes when stabilized.
